title: No serde feature on cache-friendly result types — non-negotiable #6 says SHOULD support serde behind a feature flag
description:
pkix-ct/Cargo.toml, all public types

Non-negotiable #6 in AGENTS.md:

> They [public result/error types] SHOULD support `serde::Serialize +
> Deserialize` behind a `serde` feature flag for cross-process /
> persistent caches.

`pkix-ct` already has `serde` as an optional dep (gated on
`log-list-json` for the input JSON parsing). It does NOT expose
`Serialize/Deserialize` on its public types behind a `serde` feature
flag for caller use.

Public types that should support serde behind a feature:

- `Error` — for cross-process error reporting
- `SignedCertificateTimestamp` — for cache keys, audit logs, replay
- `SctList` — for the same
- `CtLog` and `CtLogList` — for caller-side trust store
  persistence
- `MerkleAuditPath` — for proof persistence (a caller cached a
  proof and wants to replay it)
- `SignedTreeHead` — for STH cache (extremely common: a TLS server
  caches the latest STH it has verified)

Today none of these derive Serialize/Deserialize. Caller wanting to
cache a parsed SCT has to:

- Re-parse from the wire bytes on every cache lookup (slow), OR
- Define their own caller-side mirror struct with serde + a
  conversion impl on both sides (boilerplate), OR
- Cache the SCT wire bytes and re-parse on hit (acceptable, but
  silly given the struct is already in memory).

Recommendation: add a `serde` feature:

```toml
[features]
serde = ["dep:serde", "der/serde", ...]
```

Derive `Serialize + Deserialize` on every public data type behind
`#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(...))]`. This is a one-line
change per type plus a feature in Cargo.toml.

Cost: ~10 derive lines, one new feature, zero runtime cost (only
compile-time and dep-graph cost for opted-in callers).

Benefit: cross-process caches, persistent STH stores, audit logs,
replay testing all become trivial.

Priority P1 because adding `Serialize/Deserialize` derives later is
technically non-breaking but the cache-key contract has implications
for which fields are present and what their types are; deciding
this BEFORE callers have built workarounds is a lot easier than
after.
close_reason:
Fixed. serde now covers the six public types behind the existing feature flag, and the one with an invariant does not get a naive derive.

One correction to the bead: it says "Today none of these derive Serialize/Deserialize". Error already did -- the serde feature existed and was documented as covering the Error type. The other six did not, so the substance holds.

Five are plain derives: SignedCertificateTimestamp, SctList, MerkleAuditPath, SignedTreeHead, CtLog. Checked each before deriving -- they hold only u8, u64, [u8; 32], Vec<u8> and String (no foreign der/spki types needing a wire helper), and all have infallible new() constructors guarding no invariant, so a derive skips nothing.

CtLogList is the one that mattered, and a naive derive would have introduced a security hole while closing this bead. CtLogList::insert enforces RFC 6962 3.2 (log_id == SHA-256(key_der)) and rejects a mismatch as a corrupted source. A derived Deserialize populates the private BTreeMap field directly and never calls insert. Because CtLogList::get(log_id) is how a caller maps a parsed SCT back to a trusted log key, an entry filed under a key that does not match it means verifying an SCT against the WRONG KEY -- exactly what 3.2 exists to prevent. And persisting/reloading is the path an attacker reaches by editing a cache on disk, which is the very use case the bead asks serde for, so the check must re-run on deserialize rather than only at first parse.

Implementation: serde(into = "Vec<CtLog>", try_from = "Vec<CtLog>"), with TryFrom routing every entry through insert. It serializes as a bare sequence rather than a map, because the key IS SHA-256(key_der) of the value it indexes -- storing it would duplicate bytes already present and let the two copies disagree.

Tests: pkix-ct/tests/serde_types.rs, 8 cases -- a round trip per type, one asserting the wire form is a sequence with no redundant key, one asserting indexed lookup still works after the round trip (so the key is rebuilt), and a_log_list_whose_log_id_does_not_match_its_key_is_rejected.

Verified by mutation: swapping the into/try_from for a plain derive makes the tampered list LOAD SUCCESSFULLY and the test fail. That is the hole, demonstrated.

Added serde_json to dev-dependencies for a concrete format; the crate itself still names no wire format.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, typos, 2356 tests, and cargo hack check --workspace --feature-powerset --depth 2 over 241 combinations with no errors -- run workspace-wide this time, after a single-crate powerset let a cross-crate feature regression through earlier today.
